placements.why: The envelope's entire content — a spectrograph's calibration value and its verification against reference plates — names an organizational category (calibration/verification work) that nothing in the supplied (empty) strata covers. Both existing strata and narrative structure were supplied empty, so no reuse was possible; this category is legible on its own as the umbrella the calibration-verification theme below sits under.
placements.title: instrument calibration and verification against reference standards as an organizational category
placements.frame: does this content concern establishing, checking, or maintaining an instrument's calibrated state against a named reference standard?

placements.title: an instrument's calibration counts as settled only once checked against a named reference standard
placements.frame: was this calibration checked against a specific, named reference standard, and does the verification claim hold across the instrument's full operating range?
placements.why: src-1 states the Kestrelwood spectrograph's 88.4 MHz calibration and its verification against the June reference plates holding across the full observing band; src-2 and src-3 restate the same instrument identity and calibration-verification fact in labelled-field form. This is a recurring subject future calibration envelopes (other instruments, other reference checks, other bands) would keep feeding, not a one-time measurement report — the measurement (88.4 MHz, June plates) is the evidence, the theme is that calibration is established via reference-standard verification. No existing leaf was supplied to reuse, so this is minted fresh under the newly-minted Calibration strata.
